name: Congo Natty
editorial_article: Congo Natty, the influential alias of British producer and musician Michael West (also known as Rebel MC), is a central figure in the history and evolution of Jungle music. Born in London, West first gained prominence in the late 1980s with the pop-rap project Double Trouble, notably scoring a hit with "Street Tuff." However, his most profound and enduring cultural impact lies in his transition to the burgeoning jungle scene in the early 1990s. As Congo Natty, he became a primary architect of the genre, effectively fusing the rapid, complex breakbeats of early hardcore with the spiritual weight and heavy sub-bass aesthetics of roots reggae and dub sound system culture. \n\nHis work as Congo Natty is deeply ideological, often framing Jungle as a modern, UK-born extension of Jamaican roots music—a "re-boot" for a new, diverse generation. His landmark 2013 album *Jungle Revolution*, released on Big Dada and mixed by legendary dub producer Adrian Sherwood, serves as a definitive statement of this philosophy. The project captures the essence of his sound: blood, fire, righteous anger, and intense religious fervor, all anchored by razor-sharp production. Throughout his career, West has remained a vital mentor and collaborator within British electronic music, consistently highlighting the interconnected lineage between jungle, dubstep, and grime. His contributions remain foundational to the understanding of jungle not just as a rhythmic evolution, but as a spiritual and social movement within the UK underground.

editorial_bio: Congo Natty, a pioneering figure of British Jungle music, represents the fusion of sound system culture and rapid-fire breakbeats. Known for his deeply spiritual and ideological approach, he continues to bridge the gap between classic roots reggae and contemporary UK bass music.
